doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Back in Cleveland: drugstore and first club production
summary: He worked at Curlander's drug store, sang some local gigs and produced a show at Cedar Gardens.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What did you do after you left the band?
Went home to Cleveland. Got a job.
What kind of job?
I worked in the drugstore that I grew up. He was on the corner. Curlander’s Drug Store. That was the name of the fellow who owned it.
How old were you at this point?
Huh?
How old were you at this point?
At that point, I guess I must have been like almost 30 years old, not quite.
In your 20s.
I was in my 20s, late 20s.
Were you discouraged? Did you feel like, my voice is on this hit song, it’s being played all over the country, and here I am working at a drug store – what the hell’s happening?
No, no.
That was not your . . .
I didn’t even think about it. Keep going on.
Keep going on.
No turning back. I still had a job to do.
At the drug store.
Yes.
But were you also singing gigs in Cleveland?

I did do a couple of little places that used to know me. I’d go by and sing there. Then, when I was home, they’d ask me to do gigs for them and how much did I charge and like that. So I did. I went. One guy had the club – honey, you’d know. You don’t know the name of the club either, where Goo-Goo Eyes and myself – this was a blues singer . . .
This period when you’re back in Cleveland, you’re regrouping your strength and determination . . .
[recording interrupted]
I did that club. That’s where I did my first production. I produced a show . . .
At the Cedar Gardens.
. . . at Cedar Gardens. It was like an old-time burlesque.
Oh yeah. You produced a whole show with dancers.
No, I don’t think it was a whole show. It was – Cedar Gardens was a nightclub, always a nightclub.
The Cotton Club she’s talking about. Jeannie Scott: The Cotton Club [?]. Jimmy Scott: The Cotton Club, that was something else. That was downtown. That was downtown.
